title: Enterprise model onboarding intake: priority matrix & gating workflow
creator: Priya Raman
description:
Background: Enterprise customers are requesting a faster, auditable path for getting new model variants into Redwood's catalog (new models, minor/major version pins, and deprecation notices). Current intake is ad hoc — PMs triage emails, eng teams rebuild benchmarks from scratch, and compliance reviews happen late. This ticket defines a structured intake form, a numerical priority matrix tailored to enterprise needs, and a set of gating steps (eval gates, security/compliance gate, rollout plan) so requests can be triaged consistently and SLA'd for enterprise customers.

Goals:
- Reduce time-to-decision for enterprise model requests from ~3 weeks to <= 5 business days for initial triage.
- Provide a clear, reproducible scoring rubric so PM/Eng/SRE/Trust can align on priority.
- Define required artifacts and an automated checklist that prevents missing compliance or license review during onboarding.
- Establish explicit rules for version pinning and deprecation notices (timeline + rollback criteria).

Proposed intake form (minimum required fields):
- Requestor & company (name, email, account id)
- Model identifier and provenance (HF model-id or self-hosted artifact link)
- License and export/control notes (Apache2/BSD/MIT/other)
- Intended usage (chat, retrieval-augmented generation, embeddings, reranking)
- Expected qps & latency SLOs, estimated token mix (prompt vs completion)
- Data residency or encryption requirements
- Reason for request: new capability | cost reduction | regulatory requirement | control of hallucination | version pin
- Required artifacts: model card, initial eval set (small), reference prompts, failure mode examples
- Security contact & compliance owner

Priority scoring matrix (example weights, totals 0-100):
- Enterprise contract impact (committed spend / SLA necessity): 0-30
- Regulatory / data residency requirement: 0-20
- Security / licensing risk (open vs restricted): 0-15 (higher number = higher urgency if restrictive but needed)
- Latency / infra complexity (GPU/quantization needs): 0-10
- Expected unit-cost delta (savings or increased cost): 0-10
- Quality delta on key evals (ROUGE/accuracy/embedding similarity): 0-15
Decision thresholds (first-pass):
- Score >= 70: High priority — empaneled review within 3 business days, engineering PoC allocation, security review kickoff.
- Score 45-69: Medium — PM-led follow-up to gather missing artifacts, schedule engineering triage in next cycle.
- Score < 45: Low — backlog; notify requester with recommended self-serve guidance.

Gating workflow (linear steps):
1) Intake received -> system creates ticket and auto-populates checklist from provided fields.
2) PM triage (2 business days): confirm artifacts present, run auto-license check, run small smoke eval on standardized prompt set (automated job).
3) If smoke eval passes (quality + safety heuristics): schedule engineering bench test (quantization viability, memory footprint) and security/compliance review in parallel.
4) Eval gates: must pass safety heuristics (toxicity, PII leakage score thresholds), and meet minimum quality thresholds on enterprise prompts.
5) If gate failures: document failure mode, suggest mitigations (instruction tuning, prompt templates, rate limiting). Create follow-up ticket with owner.
6) Approved models: create catalog entry with version pin policy, rollout plan and deprecation policy.

Version pinning policy (enterprise):
- Customer can request pin to a specific major.minor version for up to 12 months.
- Minor updates (patch-level) can be auto-approved if they are backward compatible; major upgrades require re-eval and opt-in.
- Pins require explicit release notes and a safety/regression comparison to the platform-default model.

Deprecation & rollback policy:
- 60-day notice for planned deprecations for enterprise-pinned versions unless security/legal issues necessitate immediate action.
- Provide migration guidance and a compatibility matrix.
- Automatic rollback criteria: >5% increase in user-facing error rate or >10% drop in key quality metric within canary windows.

Operational artifacts required before rollout:
- Model card (link)
- Benchmark results (unit-cost and latency at representative qps)
- Security assessment summary and remediation plan
- Owner + rollback playbook
- Privacy/data residency attestation

Automation suggestions (follow-ups):
- Intake UI that computes priority score on submit and blocks low-completeness submissions.
- CI jobs to run smoke evals and upload results to ticket.
- Template PRs for catalog metadata (automatically generated from intake).

Success metrics:
- Median time to initial triage decision <= 5 business days.
- 90% of enterprise onboarding requests include required artifacts on first submission.
- Reduction in ad-hoc security findings during onboarding by 50% year-over-year.
acceptance_criteria: Intake form draft exists and is published to Confluence with example inputs
Priority scoring matrix documented and approved by PM/Eng/Security
Automation tickets created for smoke eval job and license check (ENG backlog items referenced)
Pilot onboard 2 enterprise model requests using new flow and capture time-to-decision metrics
